standard.title: Geosynthetics — Polypropylene Multifilament Woven Geobags for Coastal and Waterways Protection — Specification
standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, sampling methods, and test procedures for geobags manufactured from polypropylene (PP) multifilament woven geotextiles. These geobags are permeable, synthetic containers designed to be filled with sand or soil for use in hydraulic and civil structures, such as river training works, bank revetments, groynes, coastal embankments, and artificial reefs to prevent soil erosion and manage floods. Woven slit-film geotextiles (made from flat tape-like yarns) are explicitly prohibited from use under this standard for permanent erosion control.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Geo Textiles (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all Polypropylene Multifilament Woven Geobags must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to be legally manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India. Export-only products conform to buyer specifications but are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic geotextiles.
requirements: Geobag rolls and prefabricated bundles must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) permanently printed or tagged, detailing the manufacturer's licence number (CM/L).
The standard classifies geobags into two varieties based on nominal mass per unit area: Type 1 (nominal mass 200 g/m²) and Type 2 (nominal mass 300 g/m²).

The raw PP multifilament woven fabric/geotextile must conform to the requirements of Clause 4.1.1. The polyester/polypropylene stitching thread used for geobag pre-fabrication must satisfy Clause 4.3, verified via supplier certificates.

Type 2 geobags must meet a minimum wide-width tensile strength of 80 kN/m in the Machine Direction (MD) and 70 kN/m in the Cross-Machine Direction (CD). Design elongation at maximum load must not exceed 25 percent in either direction.
Prefabricated joints and seams on the geobags must exhibit high efficiency, retaining a seam strength equal to at least 50 percent of the actual parent fabric tensile strength.
Type 2 geobags must satisfy a minimum trapezoidal tear strength of 1500 N in MD and 1300 N in CD, alongside a minimum CBR puncture resistance of 900 N.
Type 2 geobags must maintain water permeability at 100 mm water head of >= 18 l/m²/s, and the Apparent Opening Size (AOS) must be <= 250 microns.

The geobags must undergo 500 hours of continuous ultraviolet light exposure in a Xenon-arc apparatus (per IS 13162 Part 2). After exposure, the fabric must retain at least 80 percent of its original tensile strength in both machine and cross-machine directions.

Geobag dimensions must satisfy specified ranges: small geobags (nominal size 1.0 m x 0.7 m) and large geobags (nominal size 2.0 m x 1.5 m) must conform to design lengths, widths, and nominal sand-filled volumes.
